title: Learning of Chick Webb's death in Chicago
summary: Jones says friends hid the news of Webb's death for two days, and that Webb later appeared to him in a dream.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Back to Chick. When Chick Webb died we were in Chicago, staying on 39th Street, and they wouldn't tell me in two days, because they knew good and well I would go to pieces. Nobody would tell me that Chick Webb was dead. You know how I always go over my newspaper. They wouldn't give me nothing. Flagg at that time was there before he went to the DuSable. He was a bellboy that became the manager and built that hotel. They wouldn't have a newspaper in my room. They filed my radio off so I couldn't get nothing on the radio, because they knew good and well I would split to go to Baltimore. Later on something happened that was a phenomenon. I was in Dayton, Ohio, and I just saw Andy Kirk a couple of days ago... This man appeared to me in a dream, stood right over me and told me something that I have never been able to divulge to nobody. But from the time up until now it has given me strength, because this man was remarkable. Nobody that played with him appreciated him till after he died. They didn't know what a great man he was. I always wanted to do play Excerpts of Chick Webb. I have records and I've tried to get them to peoples -
We must do that some time.
